A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' LLM-guided short-text clustering work, renamed from TWIST to LeBoT. The main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original clustering experiments, sensitivity analyses, comparisons among LLMs, convergence measurements, and MLP distillation results.

after.justification: V2 reports original clustering results, expanded comparisons across embedders, selection-quality diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, and distillation accuracy and timing measurements.

M1.justification: The underlying procedure remains medoid selection, one-hot representative initialization, LLM selection of similar candidates, normalized mean-pooling updates, and retrieval using concatenated embeddings and constructed vectors. Both versions also describe MLP distillation. Renaming TWIST to LeBoT and adding Algorithms 1–3 clarify the existing procedure without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both retain Bank77, CLINC150, Mtop, Massive, GoEmo, and StackOverflow, plus ArxivS2S and Reddit for tuning. Intent, emotion, and programming-question clustering remain covered under the same emerging-data and unlabeled GCD scenarios. Changes to full-dataset distillation concern sampling and experimental design within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 substantially revises comparator membership. Emerging-data comparisons remove SCCL and LLMEdgeRefine, add IDAS comparisons with and without known K across additional backbones, and add SPILL comparisons for BERT and MiniLM. The GCD K-means table removes IDAS and Plain while retaining IntentGPT, LOOP, ALUP, and GLEAN.

E3.justification: The reported initial dimension changes from 2,048 to 1,024, tuning switches from Qwen to Gemma, and TF-IDF replaces Instructor among evaluated representations. Distillation uses 3,080 rather than 5,780 Bank77 examples and 4,500 rather than 7,650 CLINC150 examples, and removes the full-dataset StackOverflow experiment. V2 also introduces candidate-selection and LLM-selection accuracy metrics.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses separating candidate retrieval quality from LLM selection quality across embedders and LLMs (Appendices F/H, Tables 9/11), measures dimensionality growth, and tests initial dimensions across evaluation datasets (Figure 2). Distillation and existing sensitivity analyses are revised. HDBSCAN variants of several dimensionality, neighbor, iteration, and LLM comparisons are removed, although main HDBSCAN evaluation remains.

E5.justification: Both retain five K-means seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting in the main emerging-data table. V2 removes v1's explicit disclosure of one representation-construction run with a fixed seed and one HDBSCAN run. This reduces statistical reporting detail without establishing a change in the actual number of runs.

E6.justification: Results are substantially revised through new TF-IDF, IDAS, selection-quality, and timing entries, alongside removed comparisons and updated scores. Under revised settings, MiniLM's emerging-data mean NMI/ACC changes from 69.60/57.77 (v1 Table 5) to 70.12/58.43 (v2 Table 3). Bank77 distillation K-means changes from 83.80/73.58 to 81.44/68.99 (v1 Table 8; v2 Table 5), with fewer LLM-guided training examples. These are results under changed conditions.

T1.justification: V1 provides an idealized identical-vector proposition and omits its proof. V2 reformulates assumptions around clusters defined by the selection function, defines preference preservation through similarity inequalities, and supplies mathematical arguments. New Appendix A introduces a generalized representation and Proposition 2 concerning preservation under representative reduction and candidate selection, including a shared-representative condition.

C1.justification: V2 makes direct encoding of LLM preferences the leading contribution and adds an explicit comparative claim of reduced dependence on embedder choice. Its conclusion claims the greatest robustness across embedders, extending v1's compatibility and low-resource claims. Training-free, label-free, unknown-K construction, competitive performance, and scalability claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations linking performance differences to candidate quality, richer E5 representations, and Llama's less accurate selections. It explains inconsistent LLM preferences as motivation for pooling and iteration. Limitations now identify candidate retrieval as the remaining dependence on the embedder and suggest in-context learning for specialized domains, extending v1's more general capability caveats.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit pseudocode, clarifies that final BoT vectors alone are clustered, reports per-text inference times, and changes the documented code-access link. It removes v1's greedy-decoding and candidate-batching explanations and the discontinued Instructor prompts. These are documentation and access changes around a largely retained implementation.

R1.justification: The literature base and distinction between refining existing embeddings and constructing new vectors are largely retained. V2 categorizes training-free approaches into text enrichment and embedding post-processing, revises ALUP/GLEAN discussion, and drops several model/algorithm references. Table 2 also newly marks IDAS as fine-tuned, inconsistently with its training-free description in Section 2.

P1.justification: The title, method name, and dominant terminology change, with extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition, method description, and conclusion. Experimental presentation is reorganized around K-means and embedder robustness, while the appendices are substantially expanded and restructured.

P2.justification: V1's detailed workflow figure is replaced by a conceptual illustration and three algorithm displays. V2 restructures the main comparison tables, adds diagnostic tables and plots, redraws LLM and sensitivity charts, and moves detailed HDBSCAN results and prompts into the appendices. These changes substantially alter how the evidence and procedure are presented.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity and support through explicit algorithms, conditional mathematical arguments, comparisons across weaker embedders, and selection-quality diagnostics. Timing measurements also strengthen the scalability discussion. These gains are tempered by removed comparator and robustness results, omitted run and decoding details, and conflicting IDAS fine-tuning descriptions in Table 2 and Section 2. The net improvement is useful but limited.
